title: Bluetooth LE sensors frequently unavailable
body:
### The problem

I have a bunch of Xiaomi Mijia (LYWSD03MMC) climate sensors throughout my house flashed with the ATC firmware using the HA BLE format. Up until 2022.9 I was using the custom integration Passive BLE Monitor to integrate them all into HA. When using the custom integration I never noticed my sensors being unavailable, but since switching to the new BT Home integration they are constantly becoming unavailable.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.9

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

n/a

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

BT Home

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bthome

### Diagnostics information

Not available for BT Home

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Nothing BT Home or bluetooth related
```


### Additional information

Screenshot to show frequent gaps in availability for one of my sensors.

![Screenshot 2022-09-10 104629](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/67965669/189488553-a66f4722-8de6-46fd-8b21-0ccc3515f4c5.png)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
That should be more than ok. BLE monitor won’t let sensors go into unavailable state, but it probable didn’t update either. The Bluetooth integration works a bit different and will go faster into unavailable state. To check why this happens in your case, there are some things you can check.

Can you check if bringing the sensor closer to your Bluetooth adapter makes a difference? 

And can you enable debug logging for the Bluetooth integration and the BTHome integration. Post a log here. I want to check if HA receives BLE advertisements in the same interval as you send them.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Its likely they are quiet for so long they get removed from Dbus so they end up going unavailable.

I think the solution would be to subclass the coordinator
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/27e8e40968c3d7ecc189802725a7c26681da3d4b/homeassistant/components/bluetooth/passive_update_processor.py#L84

and override the available property with something that checks last_seen instead
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/27e8e40968c3d7ecc189802725a7c26681da3d4b/homeassistant/components/bluetooth/update_coordinator.py#L43

maybe something like


```python
@property 
def available(self):
  return time.monotonic() - self.last_seen  < UNAVAILABLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: But the question is why it is silence for so long in the first place, at least for the BTHome sensor. It broadcasts every 2.5 seconds.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Thinking about it some more, it might more sense to only override available in the entity instead since the coordinator will never update again once it goes unavailable until it gets a new advertisement 

You'll probably also need an async_track_time_interval to periodically check since you will need something to actually set it unavailable when it exceeds the timeout since there is nothing to update the state when there are no advertisements coming in.

That would be a bit more efficient as well if you store it as an attribute and reset it on advertisement as well since you don't have a time.montonic call every time the property is checked.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Running BLE monitor and the Bluetooth integration at the same time can be problematic. Try to set BLE monitor to “active scan” to have at least both integrations running in the same scanning mode.

BLE monitor sets the BLE scanner to passive scanning, while the Bluetooth integration uses active scanning (on most systems). This will confuse the adapter, so try to use both integrations in the same scanning mode. 

BLE monitor normally wins this battle, so that could explain why BLE monitor continues to work and the xiaomi-ble integration not.

comments.body: Different values are related to the averaging per minute, that BLE monitor does. BLE monitor therefore only updates once per minute. Xiaomi-ble doesn’t do averaging and will update more often (depending on the sensor broadcast interval of course)

> I have removed one of them from Passive BLE monitor to ensure it is not related to multiple integrations trying to connect to the same device, which didn’t solve the problems.

Most BLE integrations, like Xiaomi (except battery of the MiFlora), Qingping, BTHome, etc, do not connect to the devices, they just listen to BLE advertisements that are send out into the air. Even active scanning is not "connecting to a device", it just sending out a message into the wild "sensors, give me more data". So, both HA BLE integrations as BLE monitor can listen to the same sensor, as long as they are capable of using the same Bluetooth adapter. And that is where the issue can be, as explained above. 

But @reporter is saying that he has removed BLE monitor, so that can't be the issue, In the log, I see data coming in from 
- US Bath
- Office
- DSBath
- Guest BR
- Nursery
- Den

Are these all the BTHome sensors you have? Which one was unavailable?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
You could also try enabling debug logs for `bleak`.  If they are coming into `bleak` but not making it to `homeassistant.components.bluetooth` then thats probably a bug in the bluetooth integration.

If they aren't coming into `bleak` then it is probably a bug in the kernel, BlueZ, or the bluetooth adapter itself which would be really unfortunate as there wouldn't be anything we could change to resolve it.  You could also check diagnostics to see if the device still appears on the bus when its unavailable or not

I'm hoping its the former as that should be solvable. I'd expect thats the case since the esp proxies are showing the same issue according to https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/78195#issuecomment-1243928102

But there are so many different reports with different setups in this issue they may all be different problems.  Unfortunately none of my test system show any of these behaviors, however I don't have any BTHome devices (just about every other bluetooth integration though)

Additionally 2022.8.x didn't report unavailability due to an issue with bleak so this could have been a problem in 2022.8.x but it would have presented as the sensor not updating, not going unavailable.
